questions.prompt: Compare the minutes waited to see a nurse. Which statement uses all the values correctly?

content.title: minutes waited to see a nurse

content.text: A = Clinic A; B = Clinic B.

options.label: A
options.text: The groups have no value in common.

options.label: B
options.text: Each group has two values at least 10; their values overlap.

options.label: C
options.text: Every value in A is higher than every value in B.

options.label: D
options.text: Only A has two values at least 10.

support.hint: Check each statement against both rows, including any values the groups share.

stuck.introduction: Compare the groups one feature at a time.
steps: Write Clinic A's values and Clinic B's values on separate lines.
Mark values that appear in both groups, then count values at least 10 in each group. Include 10 itself.
Check every part of each statement. Reject a statement if either part disagrees with the data.

questions.prompt: At a clinic, Yes means the case got a checkup. Which percentages answer: What share within each group met the goal?

content.text: A = Clinic A; B = Clinic B.

options.label: A
options.text: A 20% and B 40%; compare the No shares.

options.label: B
options.text: A 80% and B 60%; divide by each group total.

options.label: C
options.text: A 40% and B 30%; divide by all 20 cases.

options.label: D
options.text: A 57% and B 43%; divide by all 14 Yes cases.

support.hint: A share within a group uses that group's total, including both Yes and No cases.

stuck.introduction: Build a separate checkup percentage for each clinic.
steps: For Clinic A, add Yes and No to find its total number of cases.
Divide A's Yes count by A's total and multiply by 100. Repeat using only Clinic B's counts.
Compare your two percentages with the options, checking that each denominator represents the requested group.
